strategies.name: ema_support_resistance_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: After the first 5 to 15 minutes, use the 5-minute chart to identify support; enter when price bounces off the 13 EMA acting as initial support, or later from a deeper support such as the 200 EMA / demand zone when support is confirmed by price action.
strategies.exit_summary: Take profit quickly as price moves from support toward resistance; the speaker repeatedly emphasizes getting in and out, not overstaying, and exiting at resistance or after a short favorable move.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for the first 5 to 15 minutes to establish support, then enter on the bounce off the 13 EMA
variants.target_note: exit into the quick move / at resistance
variants.transcript_quote: time your entries once you have allowed the first 5 to 15 minutes to pass ... look at this indicator the 13 EMA in this example on the 5 minute chart

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter when price bounces from deeper support at the 200 EMA after the 13 EMA loses support status
variants.target_note: exit on the short move up toward resistance
variants.transcript_quote: this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA once the 13 EMA gave up its support status

result.enumeration_note: One scalping skeleton is taught repeatedly with compatible variants: 13 EMA support bounce and deeper 200 EMA / demand-zone bounce. The late 'big move' after losing 200 EMA support is treated as the same short-entry scalp family because the exit logic remains a quick in-and-out move, not a separate fully-executed strategy.
